The Book of Famous Caves The Raccoon Log When I first encountered the cave, I knew it was something special. Locals called it the Raccoon Log, for reasons they would not explain. I had to see it for myself, and was not disappointed. Like many caves, this began as not much more than a hole in the ground.
《名洞志 浣熊木 》 初见这座洞穴时，我就知道它非同寻常。当地人管它叫「浣熊木」，却不肯说缘由。我必须亲眼看看，所幸没有失望。和许多洞穴一样，它起初也不过是地上的一个窟窿。

I skipped breakfast that morning and took only what I needed from my camp. The hole was slim, and it would be difficult already to get in and out. The last thing I needed was a full stomach.

	I squeezed my way down, one hand on my torch and the other feeling for handholds. I had to be sure that I would be able to ascend, and well, from this book you can see that I succeeded. Always come prepared.

那天早上我没吃早饭，只从营地带上必需品。洞口狭窄，进出本就困难，我最不需要的就是胃里塞得满满当当。

	我侧身挤下去，一手持火把，一手摸索可以攀附的地方。我必须确认自己还能爬回去，诸位也看到了，我成功了。永远，要有备而来。

Where was I? Oh, right. I slowly descended until I hit a relatively flat, dirt floor. It was muddy, having rained the day before, and trails where water had run were visible leading over ledges, down thin cracks that spiraled into darkness. I would not want to be here in the rain.

	A narrow path wound into the distance, a rock wall on one side and a crevice on the other. I walked for quite a while, surprised at the amount of relatively flat ground.

我说到哪了？哦，对。我缓缓下到一处相对平坦的泥地。前一日下过雨，地面泥泞，还能看到水流留下的痕迹，越过岩沿，钻进旋向黑暗的细缝。我可不想在下雨天待在这里。

	一条窄路蜿蜒伸向远方，一侧是岩壁，另一侧是裂隙。我走了相当长一段，意外于这里竟有这么多平坦的地面。

I held my torch closer to the ground, and found that the stone was chiseled, made intentionally flat by someone.

	At last, I came to the room that gave this cave its name. A small round chamber glistened with moisture, and on the far wall was a hole. Human skeletons lined the wall, most leaning as if to get some rest before continuing on.

我把火把凑近地面，发现石头有凿痕，是有人刻意磨平的。

	终于，我来到了给这座洞命名的那个房间。一间小小的圆形石室，湿气晶莹，远端墙上有一个洞。人类骸骨沿墙排列，大多斜倚着，仿佛是在继续赶路前歇上一歇。

Cautiously, I held my torch up to the hole and the other side lit up as the light reflected off of pieces of gold and silver. 

	The hole was not much bigger than a head, and some of the treasure seemed within reach.

	Being a man of wisdom, I recognized that this was too easy. Gold and untold treasure within reach, and yet, none had been taken. I peered closer at the hole and noticed something odd.

我谨慎地把火把举到洞口，火光映在对面，闪闪发亮，是成堆的金银。 

	洞口不过一颗头颅大小，有些财宝似乎伸手可及。

	我自认还算有几分明智，立刻就明白：这未免太容易了。金银与数不清的财宝近在咫尺，却一件都没被取走。我凑近细看，发现了一丝异样。

A small stone lay in the hole that should have been knocked away by any attempt to reach into it. I grabbed a torch from the ground, where one of the skeletons lay, and slowly slid it into the hole, lightly nudging the loose stone.

	With a crack, the torch was pinned against the stone, a thin vertical slab having slid downward to crush it. I stepped backwards, ears listening intently. I decided to let out a muffled gasp of mock pain.

洞里横着一块小石头，任何人伸手进去都该先把它碰开才对。我拾起地上骸骨旁的一支火把，缓缓探进洞里，轻轻拨了拨那块松石。

	咔的一声！火把被死死卡住，一块薄薄的竖石板骤然落下，将它压断。我后退一步，竖起耳朵。随后，我刻意憋出一声闷哼，假装被砸中了。

Within moments I heard footsteps, slow and lumbering, like no human I had ever heard. It was then that I noticed the skeletons, all of them, were missing an arm.

	Had the villagers sent me into a trap? Surely it was no human on the other side of that wall. Something was amiss, and I would do best not to find out what. As quietly as I could, I ran down the passage, towards the entrance.

片刻之后，我听见了脚步声，缓慢、沉重，绝不是我听过的任何人类脚步。也就在这时，我才注意到：所有骸骨，都缺了一条手臂。

	难道村民把我诓进了陷阱？墙的那一边，绝无可能是人类。有什么不对劲，而最好的选择就是不去查明。我尽可能地放轻脚步，沿通道朝洞口狂奔。

A shrill scream echoed down the halls behind me; the cry of something robbed of its prey, perhaps. I nearly slammed into the cave wall as I skidded to a stop at the entrance. I climbed. As fast as I could, I climbed, and I did not look down. I could hear something approaching from below.

	When I reached the top, I dropped my torch into the hole, and for a moment saw a large face staring back at me. I decided new camping gear was more than overdue, and ran with all my might, leaving my supplies behind me.

一声尖啸在身后的厅道里回荡，也许是被夺走了猎物的什么东西在嚎叫。我在洞口刹住脚，险些撞上岩壁。我往上爬。拼命地爬，绝不往下看。我能听到有什么东西正从下方逼近。

	爬到顶时，我把火把丢进了洞里，火光一闪，一张巨大的脸正仰望着我。我当即决定：该换一套新露营装备了，非常该了。我丢下所有辎重，用尽全身力气狂奔而去。
res#60470/whatIHaveToSay[8]
Start

That, dear reader, is why you should always be suspicious when a group of people hides something from you. True, my own folly and sense of adventure led me there to begin with, and it nearly cost me everything.
亲爱的读者，这就是为什么，当一群人拼命向你隐瞒什么时，你永远都该起疑心。诚然，是我自己的愚蠢和冒险心把我引到了那里，它几乎让我失去了一切。
